text:
Maya (Support): FYI customer report: PROD intermittent 504s + increased p50 started ~10:15 UTC. They see a lot of cross-region routing to us-west despite client in eu-west. Suspect fallback triggered by health checks. Sample req ids: r12345, r12346. Can eng-platform take a look?

Priya (Eng-Platform): Got it. Do you have the probe logs / routing decision traces? Also which failover policy are they on (aggressive/cautious/custom)?

Maya (Support): Paste of probe-agent logs from 10:14-10:18 UTC (redacted):
```
[10:14:03] probe-agent(eu-west): sent heartbeat to hc-eu-01 -> 200
[10:14:04] probe-agent(eu-west): sent heartbeat to hc-eu-02 -> timeout
[10:14:05] probe-agent(eu-west): nat-ip-change detected (10.20.5.13 -> 52.14.22.9)
[10:14:06] probe-agent(eu-west): sent heartbeat to hc-eu-02 -> timeout
[10:14:07] healthcheck-service: region eu-west marked UNHEALTHY (3 misses)
[10:14:08] routing-service: failover trigger -> route -> us-west
```
Looks like probe misses + NAT IP rotation.

Jon (SRE): We saw the same NAT rotation earlier today. Probe agents in eu-west are using a short-lived pool and NAT IP rotation causes some upstream firewalls to drop the health probe traffic until new flow is allowed. Net effect: span of 10-20s where probes appear down. The routing service treats 3 consecutive misses as region-unhealthy.

Priya (Eng-Platform): That explains it. The tenant was on default failover config (conservative thresholds but zero cooldown). When eu-west flips to UNHEALTHY we immediately fallback and requests go to us-west. Two issues: (1) aggressive immediate fallback with no cooldown, (2) probe IP rotation causing false-negatives. Short-term mitigation: set region-fallback.cooldown=30s for the tenant and increase probe timeout. Longer-term: change default cooldown and add hysteresis to routing decisions.

Sam (Eng-ML): Heads up — customer's billing report shows a token spend spike after the fallback (cross-region tokens + burst capacity). We should flag billing to avoid invoicing surprises. :warning:

deploy-bot: Automated change initiated: set `region-fallback.cooldown=30s` for tenant `acct-789`. Rollout: canary 5% -> in progress.

Maya (Support): Customer provided repro steps: during a NAT rotation window, send 200 small requests with header `X-Client-Region: eu-west`. ~10-20% were routed to us-west and saw +120ms p50. They've attached HAR; I'll share to SRE offline.

Jon (SRE): Interim actions I recommend: (1) pin probe egress IPs for health checks (disable rotation) for critical tenants, (2) increase probe timeout from 2s to 5s to tolerate transient drops, (3) add 30s cooldown on failover (already applied for this tenant). I'm opening P1: ENGPLAT-4321 to implement sticky-probe-ip and routing hysteresis.

Priya (Eng-Platform): Working on PR to routing-service: add hysteresis window and require both probe AND request-level errors before global failover; test plan: simulated probe-flaps + ratelimiting. ETA: 6h to canary patch (will post changelog and monitoring deltas).

Maya (Support): Thanks team. I'll notify customer with the temporary cooldown and that we're working on a permanent fix. Escalating billing team for the spend spike. Keeping thread open for updates. :thumbsup:

Jon (SRE): Also note: patch will emit metric `route.failover.false_positive_rate` so we can track regressions.

Priya (Eng-Platform): Adding that metric and a dashboard. Will alert if >1% of failovers are followed by immediate return within 60s.

Maya (Support): Perfect — closing loop once canary is stable.
